processing: Spring leaf processed as black tea, as with other Assam orthodox or CTC production; the seasonal leaf, not a special method, sets it apart.
harvest_season: Spring: from March, with one account giving mid-March to early May. It is followed by the more prized second flush in May and June.
appearance_dry: Dark brown leaf is typical of spring Assam; the source does not describe it further.
appearance_liquor: Golden yellow, lighter than a second flush.
appearance_wet: Soft young leaf, as is typical of spring growth.
taste_profile: A lighter Assam infusion with subtle floral notes, without the distinct maltiness of the second flush.

brewing.notes: Try it plain first. It is a lighter tea than a second flush, so strong milk may bury it.

vintage_note: Usually best bought by harvest year and estate, and drunk fresh, as is typical of spring teas.
description:
Assam first flush is the spring picking from the Brahmaputra Valley, and it is not what most people mean by Assam. The state's reputation rests on dark, malty, milk-ready tea. This earlier pick is lighter and more floral.

The difference comes from the season. It is picked from about mid-March to early May, while the fuller second flush follows from mid-May to August. Processing is black tea in the usual Assam way.

In the cup, expect a lighter infusion with subtle florals. Those who want a breakfast powerhouse may find it underwhelming, so judge it as a morning tea to drink plain.

Look for a garden name, the flush and the harvest year on the label. Plenty of Assam blends give none of these, and then you cannot know what you are buying. For a direct comparison, brew it beside a second flush from the same garden.
history: Little is documented specifically about first flush as a style. It takes its name from the seasonal rhythm of Indian tea, and it stands behind the May and June second flush, considered the best quality in Assam.
